newsitem.title: UK: BA and cabin crew union to continue talks.
newsitem.headline: BA and cabin crew union to continue talks.

text.p: Talks aimed at settling the pay dispute between British Airways Plc and its biggest cabin crew union are to continue, following an initial meeting between the two sides on Wednesday.
Both the airline and the union agreed not to comment on the progress of the talks.

British government industrial relations arbitration service ACAS, which is leading the negotiations, said in a statement: "Talks between British Airways and the Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) concerning the cabin crew dispute are continuing with the assistance of ACAS, and both parties have agreed that no further statements shall be made until these talks are concluded."
The dispute over a pay restructuring plan led to a three-day strike by cabin crew earlier this month, grounding hundreds of BA flights.

Management negotiators met with officials from the TGWU's BA Stewards and Stewardesses' Association (BASSA) unit today to receive the union's alternative proposals on how to achieve the 42 million pounds ($70.5 million) savings required by the restructuring plan.
Earlier, BA chief executive Robert Ayling said he was hopeful of a deal but expected that negotiations would take some time.

"We will need time to fully evaluate the proposals. If they (the union) meet the 42 million pounds in a way that is acceptable to all parties, including the cabin crew themselves, British Airways will seek to move matters forward as quickly as possible," he said in a statement.
A T&G spokesman said the union was submitting its alternative proposals "in all seriousness" and hoped the airline would adopt them.

BASSA, the largest BA cabin crew union, has accepted in principle the need to save 42 million pounds from cabin crew costs, part of the airline's one billion pound ($1.6 billion) cost-cutting and increased efficiency drive, BA said.

BA said as long as the union proposals meet its target figure in a way acceptable to all parties, it would then seek a process to move things forward jointly with BASSA -- representing 8,500 cabin crew members -- and breakaway union Cabin Crew 89, the second cabin crew union representing 3,500 members.
Cabin Crew 89 has already accepted the pay deal.
